meta.title: If-clauses and Reported Speech
meta.subtitle: real and unreal conditions, the imperfect subjunctive, and reporting statements, questions and orders
meta.footer: Spanish Learning Program · B1 · Grammar · If-clauses and reported speech
meta.next: Next: B1 · PDF 8 — ser/estar and verbs of change

blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: make real conditions with si + present (Si llueve, me quedo en casa)
make unreal or unlikely conditions with si + imperfect subjunctive (Si tuviera dinero, viajaría)
report what someone said, asked or ordered (Dijo que vendría)
shift tenses, time words and pronouns correctly in reported speech

blocks.text: When the condition is possible or likely, use si + present indicative. The result can be present, future or imperative.

head: Pattern
Example
English
rows: Si llueve, me quedo en casa.
If it rains, I stay at home.
If you study, you will pass the exam.
If you are thirsty, drink water.
Si no te das prisa, vas a llegar tarde.
If you do not hurry, you are going to be late.
Si no ha llegado, lo llamaré.
If he has not arrived, I will call him.

blocks.title: Never a future after si
blocks.text: After si (if) you use the present, never the future: Si tengo tiempo, iré, not Si tendré tiempo, iré. (Me pregunto si vendrá is different: here si means "whether".)

blocks.title: Same as Dutch
blocks.text: Dutch als het regent, blijf ik thuis works exactly the same. The difference is only the future: Dutch also avoids als ik zal komen.
Take the ellos form of the preterite, remove -ron, and add the endings below. This works for every verb, regular or irregular.

items: Endings: -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran. The nosotros form always has an accent on the vowel before -ramos: habláramos, tuviéramos.
Verbs with a j in the preterite (decir, traer, conducir) drop the i: dijeron gives dijera, not dijiera.

blocks.text: For things that are unlikely, imaginary or contrary to fact use si + imperfect subjunctive, and the conditional in the result (see B1 PDF 1).

head: Situation
Example
English
rows: Si tuviera dinero, viajaría por el mundo.
If I had money, I would travel the world.
Si ganara la lotería, compraría una casa.
If I won the lottery, I would buy a house.
Si fuera tú, hablaría con ella.
If I were you, I would talk to her.
Si pudieras ayudarme, te lo agradecería.
If you could help me, I would be grateful.
¿Qué harías si estuvieras en mi lugar?
What would you do if you were in my place?

blocks.title: Not the conditional after si
blocks.text: The si clause never takes the conditional: Si tuviera tiempo, iría, not Si tendría tiempo, iría. Dutch speakers often make this mistake because they think of zou twice (als ik tijd zou hebben, zou ik gaan).

blocks.title: Useful with quisiera
blocks.text: Quisiera (imperfect subjunctive of querer) is a polite "I would like": Quisiera una mesa para dos. Pudiera and debiera are also used for politeness.
como si (as if) always takes the imperfect subjunctive: Habla como si fuera el jefe. (He talks as if he were the boss.)
When the introducing verb is present (dice que), nothing changes except pronouns. When it is a past tense (dijo que), the tense usually shifts back.

head: Direct speech
Reported (dijo que ...)
English
rows: She said she was going to the cinema.
Dijo que había comprado un coche. (past perfect)
He said he had bought a car.
Dijo que iría al día siguiente. (conditional)
He said he would go the next day.

blocks.title: Shift summary
bullets: preterite / present perfect to past perfect (había + participle)

blocks.text: Time and place words shift too, when the reporting happens at a different moment:

head: Direct
Reported
English
rows: He asked me if I was hungry.
She asked me where I lived.
He asked me what I wanted.
He told me to come there.
She asked me not to talk.
Me ordenó que cerrara la puerta.
He ordered me to close the door.

items: Yes/no questions use si: Preguntó si venías. Question words stay, without question marks: Preguntó cuándo llegaba.
Orders and requests use que + subjunctive. With a past introducing verb, the subjunctive is the imperfect: Me dijo que viniera. With a present introducing verb it is the present: Me dice que venga.
Common introducing verbs: decir, preguntar, contestar, responder, pedir, explicar, contar, comentar, añadir.

rows: Si fuera rico, compro un barco.
Si fuera rico, compraría un barco.
Dijo que iría al día siguiente.

blocks.text: Fill in the verb in brackets or the missing word. Answers are on the last page.

items.q: Si ______ mañana, me quedaré en casa.
items.full: Si llueve mañana, me quedaré en casa.

items.q: Si ______ dinero, viajaría por el mundo.
items.full: Si tuviera dinero, viajaría por el mundo.

items.q: Si yo ______ tú, hablaría con ella.
items.full: Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con ella.

items.q: Si ______ la lotería, compraría una casa.
items.full: Si ganara la lotería, compraría una casa.
Habla como si fuera el jefe.
Dijo que iría al día siguiente.

items.q: Dijo que ya ______ comprado el billete.
items.full: Dijo que ya había comprado el billete.
Me dijo que cerrara la puerta.
Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería chino.

items.q: If it rains, we will stay at home.
items.a: Si llueve, nos quedaremos en casa.

items.q: If I had a car, I would travel more.
He asked me where I lived.
